title: Same Context, Different Agents: A Behavioral Study of Semantic Layers, Orchestration and Compaction in Data Agents
abstract: arXiv:2610.20959v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Answering questions over heterogeneous data means combining evidence from files, databases, documents and the web. Data agents automate this, but their success depends on context. Three context-engineering techniques (CETs) help by shaping it: semantic layers describe the data, orchestration splits work among agents, and compaction condenses interaction history. Existing studies validate each CET alone, leaving open how agent behavior shapes its effect. We present a comprehensive analysis of the three CETs, alone and combined, with seven large language models (LLMs) on 1,514 long-horizon tasks from five benchmarks, covering behavior, accuracy and cost. We find that data agents without CETs form three behavior groups: investigators, premature answerers that answer without inspecting data, and early stoppers that give up. Each CET delivers its known benefit, from more investigation to smaller prompts, but only the behavior group it match

translated_title: 相同上下文，不同智能体：数据智能体中语义层、编排与压缩的行为研究
translated_abstract: 回答异构数据上的问题意味着需要整合来自文件、数据库、文档和网页的证据。数据智能体（Data Agents）可以实现这一过程的自动化，但其成败取决于上下文。三种上下文工程技术（Context-Engineering Techniques，CETs）通过塑造上下文来发挥作用：语义层用于描述数据，编排（orchestration）用于在多个智能体之间分配工作，压缩（compaction）用于精简交互历史。现有研究仅单独验证了每种CET的效果，而智能体行为如何影响其作用仍是一个悬而未决的问题。我们对这三种CET进行了全面分析，涵盖单独使用与组合使用的情形，涉及七个大语言模型（LLMs）在来自五个基准的1,514个长时程任务上的表现，考察维度包括行为、准确性和成本。我们发现，在没有CET的情况下，数据智能体会形成三种行为群体：深入调查者、不检查数据就过早作答的“过早回答者”，以及中途放弃的“过早停止者”。每种CET都带来了其已知的好处——从促使更多调查到缩小提示规模——但只有与其相匹配的行为群体……（原文摘要至此截断）
tldr: 该论文首次系统性地研究了语义层、编排与压缩三种上下文工程技术在数据智能体中单独及组合使用时的行为、准确性与成本影响，发现无这些技术的智能体会呈现调查者、过早回答者和过早停止者三种行为群体，且每种技术的收益取决于其所匹配的智能体行为群体。
en_tdlr: This paper presents the first comprehensive behavioral study of three context-engineering techniques—semantic layers, orchestration, and compaction—for data agents across seven LLMs and 1,514 long-horizon tasks, revealing that agents without these techniques fall into three behavior groups (investigators, premature answerers, and early stoppers), and that each technique's benefit depends on the agent behavior group it matches.
